subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Cervical cancer: staging, definitive chemoradiotherapy, systemic immunotherapy, bevacizumab and antibody-drug conjugates

steps.tx: Persistent infection with **high-risk human papillomavirus** genotypes 16 and 18 causes over 70% of invasive cervical cancers worldwide. Integration of viral DNA into the host genome produces continuous expression of oncoproteins E6 and E7. Viral E6 binds ubiquitin ligase E6AP to degrade tumour suppressor **p53**, while viral E7 binds and inactivates retinoblastoma protein **pRb**, deregulating cell cycle checkpoints.

steps.tx: The revised **FIGO 2018 staging** system incorporates modern cross-sectional imaging and pathological assessment into clinical cervical cancer staging. Stage IB is subdivided by maximum tumour dimension into stage **IB1** under 2 cm, stage **IB2** measuring 2 to 3.9 cm, and stage **IB3** measuring 4 cm or larger. Furthermore, detecting pelvic or para-aortic lymph node metastases automatically assigns stage IIIC.

steps.tx: The fused scans pair anatomy with glowing **sugar avid spots** marking active tumour in the pelvis and nodes higher up. A bright **cervical mass** anchors the disease below, with pelvic node spots defining **stage three C one** and para aortic node spots raising it to **stage three C two**. Seeing para aortic spread matters because it extends the radiation field and confirms imaging based staging over clinical examination alone.
steps.say: The coronal and sagittal fused images show an avid cervical mass with glowing pelvic nodes and higher para aortic nodes. Pelvic node involvement corresponds to stage three C one while para aortic involvement raises the stage to three C two. Detecting that upper spread on imaging changes management by extending the radiation field, which clinical examination alone would miss.

steps.tx: In locally advanced cervical cancer stage IB3 to IVA, standard curative therapy comprises external beam radiotherapy delivering 45 to 50 Gy with concurrent weekly **cisplatin** at 40 mg/m2, followed by high-dose-rate intracavitary **brachytherapy**. Image-guided adaptive brachytherapy delivers concentrated conformal doses to the high-risk clinical target volume while sparing the rectum, sigmoid colon, and urinary bladder.

steps.tx: In newly diagnosed locally advanced cervical cancer, the landmark phase III **KEYNOTE-A18** trial established adding **pembrolizumab** to standard concurrent chemoradiotherapy. Pembrolizumab administered concurrently with chemoradiotherapy and continued as maintenance therapy for up to 2 years significantly improved progression-free survival and overall survival, establishing immune checkpoint blockade in high-risk locally advanced disease.

steps.tx: In persistent, recurrent, or metastatic cervical cancer expressing a **combined positive score** of 1 or higher, the phase III **KEYNOTE-826** trial proved that adding **pembrolizumab** to chemotherapy with or without **bevacizumab** significantly prolongs overall survival. Chemoimmunotherapy achieved a dramatic survival benefit over chemotherapy alone, establishing this combination as first-line standard.

steps.tx: The landmark **GOG 240 trial** established that adding anti-VEGF monoclonal antibody **bevacizumab** at 15 mg/kg to cisplatin-paclitaxel or topotecan-paclitaxel doublet chemotherapy significantly prolongs overall survival in advanced cervical cancer. Adding bevacizumab improved median overall survival from 13.3 to 16.8 months, although clinicians must remain vigilant for hypertension, thromboembolism, and gastrointestinal-vaginal fistulae.

points: Indicated in recurrent, persistent, or metastatic disease

right.title: Vascular Adverse Events
points: Strict caution in patients with prior pelvic irradiation

steps.tx: **Tisotumab vedotin** is a novel **tissue factor-directed** antibody-drug conjugate approved for recurrent or metastatic cervical cancer progressing after chemotherapy. In the phase III **innovaTV 301** trial, tisotumab vedotin significantly improved overall survival compared to investigator-choice single-agent chemotherapy. Routine ocular mitigation protocols comprising vasoconstrictor and lubricating eye drops prevent class-specific ocular surface adverse events.

steps.tx: The randomized phase III **INTERLACE trial** demonstrated that delivering 6 weeks of **induction chemotherapy** with carboplatin and paclitaxel immediately prior to definitive chemoradiation significantly improves progression-free and overall survival in locally advanced cervical cancer. Five-year overall survival rose from 72% with standard chemoradiation to 80% with induction chemotherapy, establishing a new therapeutic option.
